title: Enhancing Search: Migrating From Traditional Solr Faceting to the JSON Faceting API
summary: Before the transition to Apache Solr 9, it is critical to modernize our codebase by embracing newer approaches supported by future Solr releases. Part of this transition is migrating away from legacy faceting code in favor of the JSON Facet API, which provides an alternative and more sleek solution to…
body_text: Before the transition to Apache Solr 9, it is critical to modernize our codebase by embracing newer approaches supported by future Solr releases. Part of this transition is migrating away from legacy faceting code in favor of the JSON Facet API, which provides an alternative and more sleek solution to sending facets to Solr. This project encapsulates the efforts taken to successfully migrate to this newer API, and insights into future improvements we could potentially make. Faceted Search Using ZoomInfo Faceted search is a powerful tool for users of ZoomInfo’s products, as it allows the user to navigate and filter the large sets of data that ZoomInfo offers its clients. The way it does this is by providing the option to drill down the data by filtering by attributes in the data. As shown above, the ZoomInfo interface has key facets such as Location, Management Levels, and Job Departments. After the initial search, analyzing the importance of these facets can help break down all the data a client has. These charts can help visualize to clients what facets are prevalent in their initial search, and then can help clients refine their searches. Diving deeper into ZoomInfo Marketing, we can see how selecting multiple filters allows for a smarter faceted search. Users can combine various facets to create highly targeted searches. The power of faceted search lies in its ability to provide a dynamic search experience with visuals that represent search results obtained through faceting. This helps users not only navigate through data but also discover patterns and insights within the data that might not be immediately apparent. Why JSON Facet API? Before the introduction of the JSON Facet API, Apache Solr users relied on traditional faceting methods to enhance search experiences. To understand the importance of the JSON Facet API, let’s delve into the nuances which separate the legacy methodologies from the newer implementations. Limitations of Traditional Faceting Traditional faceting methods in Apache Solr, while effective, have several drawbacks that the JSON Facet API aims to fix: Verbose Code : Constructing complex facet requests often resulted in lengthy and difficult-to-read code, reducing knowledge transferring capabilities due to the nature of the codebase. Limited Flexibility : Traditional facets come with a very rigid structure, making it difficult to create intricate, nested facets. Performance Bottlenecks : Legacy facets come with increased request latency and drastically inefficient garbage collection procedures compared to the JSON Facet API. Readability Concerns : Responses are difficult to parse and understand, especially for hierarchical facets. The nesting and structure of JSON objects is far easier to understand as opposed to the flat namespace of the legacy faceting techniques. Advantages of JSON Facet API JSON Facet API addresses these limitations and offers several advantages, making it far more favorable to adopt: Intuitive Structure : JSON is a format many are familiar with, and even for those unfamiliar with it, JSON’s inherent nested structure allows for a very natural representation of complex facet relationships. Improved Flexibility : Facet requests are easily constructed with several Java classes which provide support for constructing complicated facets with several parameters in a structured manner. Better Readability: Both the requests and responses are readable by the untrained eye, which helps improve debugging amongst developers and data interpretation. Under the Hood Analysis As mentioned above, how a SolrQuery looks under the hood varies greatly between the JSON Facet API and legacy faceting code. When a developer is debugging and viewing the state of all variables, how the SolrQuery is structured is important, and as seen below, there are clear advantages to the JSON Facet API. JSON structure provides a clean, hierarchical representation of facets. Each facet is a self-contained object with its own parameters, making it easier to understand the facet’s configuration at a glance. Easier to debug and maintain complex faceting logic, as changes and additions to facets are more straightforward. Designed with extensibility in mind, as additions in future Solr releases will be easier to integrate due to its flexible structure. This JSON structure replaces traditional parameters like: Traditional parameters are flat and become difficult for complex faceting scenarios. Query string becomes harder and harder to read with more additions. Debugging is especially challenging due to the long-winded string that SolrQuery can become. Less flexible for future enhancements due to its parameter-based approach. Solution: Embracing the JSON Facet API The JSON Facet API offers a robust solution for the issues presented by the deprecated legacy faceting solution. Providing a more intuitive, flexible, and powerful way of constructing facet queries, this API requires extensive modifications of current faceting code, as well as parsing the responses and building the appropriate responses. Let’s explore these steps in greater detail: Understanding Existing Implementation to Send Requests Legacy faceting code has a fundamentally different approach to setting the parameters of facets. Rather than working to create several instances of facets to be sent to Solr, the SolrQuery is modified itself to accommodate for facet usage, as defined by the user who made the request. Below, we see a chart which delineates the way in which legacy facets are curated and sent to Solr. Understanding Existing Response Handling After the response is received from Solr, the response must be handled accordingly. Legacy facet responses from Solr are currently equipped with functions which perform much of the heavy lifting when it comes to logic and obtaining the relevant information needed to build a valuable client response. The QueryResponse class provides methods to conveniently obtain facet fields and facet queries to prepare the final facet data for client consumption. The chart below illustrates the processes in which legacy faceting responses are handled, starting from extracting the facet results, applying logic to prepare these responses for post-processing, and building a cohesive and useful result: Reworking to follow JSON Facet API Design Pattern The JSON Facet API leverages several useful and practical classes to compartmentalize all the different types of facets used to make a developer’s life far simpler. Rather than directly manipulating the SolrQuery, the facet requests are defined through a readable Map which forms each facet in a JSON-like manner. Under the hood, we can easily read the JSON facet which will be sent to Solr, allowing for more flexibility when debugging and modifying facets. The key differences are further discussed and shown below: The SolrQuery is not modified until the JSON facet is set manually, allowing for the ability to build deeper and more complex facets to Solr. Flexibility enhancements allowed by defining multiple facet types. Clear visualization of how different facet types are incorporated into a single JSON facet map, along with their state. Handling JSON Facet Responses Contrary to the legacy code, the JSON Facet API requires a more manual approach to processing all the facet data. The flexibility of the JSON Facet API allows for more complex and varied structure, which is why the API provides lower-level access to the facet data. This gives developers more control but does require more manual processing compared to the “simpler” traditional faceting. The chart demonstrates this process, which involves extracting the JSON faceting response and drilling down on the bucket-based facets and the query facets using methods introduced exclusively for the JSON Facet API. Highlighted below is a chart showing the process and methods utilized to streamline the process: Abstraction A valuable thing to note is the idea of abstraction. When migrating from traditional faceting to the JSON Facet API in Solr, abstraction is crucial in maintaining consistency for client applications. By meticulously implementing the response processing methodologies, a developer can shield clients from the underlying changes in the faceting mechanism, ensuring that the response structure remains unchanged despite the shift in the backend implementation. Future Scope Transition to JsonQueryRequest from SolrQuery Currently, SolrQuery is used everywhere when building queries to be sent to Solr. Switching to using only JsonQueryRequest as the container holding query parameters allows greater use of the JSON Facet API, as this class contains many methods to further streamline the process of defining facets. JsonQueryRequest provides great support for the JSON Facet API, as any JsonFacetMap can be configured to be set as the facet for each request directly, removing much of the overhead associated with constructing a facet request. Old SolrQuery Approach New JsonQueryRequest Approach SolrQuery solrQuery = new SolrQuery();solrQuery.setQuery(“*:*”);solrQuery.addFacetField(“category”);solrQuery.setFacetMinCount(1);solrQuery.setRows(0); TermsFacetMap categoryFacet = new TermsFacetMap(“category”).setMinCount(1);TermsFacetMap companyFacet = new TermsFacetMap(“company”);JsonQueryRequest jsonRequest = new JsonQueryRequest() .setQuery(“*:*”) .setLimit(0) .setMinCount(5) .withFacet(“category”, categoryFacet);

title: OrioleDB Public Alpha
summary: Launching OrioleDB Public Alpha
body_text: OrioleDB Public Alpha # Today, we're releasing the Public Alpha of OrioleDB on the Supabase platform. What’s OrioleDB? # OrioleDB is a storage extension which uses Postgres' pluggable storage system. It’s designed to be a drop-in replacement for Postgres’ default Heap storage. You can read more about OrioleDB here and learn why you might choose it over the default Postgres storage engine. Limitations # This initial release is a Public Alpha and you should not use it for Production workloads. The release comes with several limitations: The release is restricted to Free organizations. You will not be able to upgrade OrioleDB projects to larger instance sizes. If you want to run OrioleDB on a larger instance we suggest following the Getting Started guide on OrioleDB’s official website. Index support is restricted to the Postgres default B-Tree index type. Other indexs like GIN/GiST/BRIN/Hash, and pgvector's HNSW/IVFFlat are not supported. Should you use it today? # At this stage, the goal of adding OrioleDB to the platform is to make it easier for testers to give feedback. If you’re running Production workloads, stick to the standard options available. Getting started and more info # To get started today, go to database.new and choose “Postgres with OrioleDB” under the "Advanced Configuration" section when launching a new database. If you want to learn more about OrioleDB and their vision for the future, check out the blog post the OrioleDB team released today .

title: A guide to sample management for modern R&D
summary: In this guide, we break down sample management into bite-sized tasks, share key principles for effective sample management, and outline what modern solutions are out there so that you can spend less time organizing and more time on your next experiment.
body_text: Summary: Sample management has gotten harder as data volumes explode and teams grow more distributed. This guide breaks it down into manageable pieces and outlines what modern solutions actually look like. With 87% of biotech leaders expecting at least 2x data growth this year, fragmented sample data isn't just messy; it actively slows down analysis and collaboration. Effective sample management means linking physical samples to their experimental context, keeping inventory connected to order management, and making all of it searchable and traceable. Modern solutions like Benchling do this by integrating registration, notebook, inventory, and results in one place, with instrument data entry automations to reduce manual work. Your manager has tasked you with the formidable job of digitally and physically organizing your lab’s samples and inventory into an intuitive and easy to maintain system of organization. Easy, right? But as you attempt to excavate the ice encrusted graveyard of samples of coworkers long gone in your lab’s ancient sample freezer and sift through expired inventory that may have been purchased at the turn of the century, you wonder if modern sample management may be harder than you think. In this guide, we break down sample management into bite-sized tasks, share key principles for effective sample management, and outline what modern solutions exist so that you can spend less time organizing and more time on your next experiment. What is sample management? Sample management is a vital part of scientific R&D, that if done right, has the potential to improve product quality and patient health. It encompasses the processes and practices involved in handling samples of materials, products, or substances throughout their lifecycle. While these practices may vary from company to company, common sample management tasks include: Sample collection: This initial step establishes standardized procedures for collecting and documenting samples, including origin, collection method, and any relevant environmental conditions. Labeling and identification: Using labels to assign identifying information, as well as the use of barcodes, ensures that each unique sample can be tracked in the lab and you’re not spending precious minutes trying to decipher half-smudged Sharpie. Storage: Storing samples under appropriate conditions preserves integrity, while optimizing storage location means you’re not digging through the lab freezer on a regular basis. Tracking and analysis: Consistent documentation of the handling of samples provides a clear record of sample movement. When analyzing samples, it’s important to follow protocols to drive consistency with results and insights so that you don’t have to repeat experiments when data is somehow misplaced. Quality control and compliance: It’s a prerequisite for effective management that samples maintain standards for quality, commonly achieved through regular audits. Regulatory and industry standards such as Good Laboratory Practice (GLP) provide guidance for creating such conditions. Disposal: Safe and compliant disposal, including records of disposed samples, ensures visibility and traceability for all parties and prevents you from having to sift through expired samples and reagents. Why you need effective sample management in the new R&D era Effective sample management practices are foundational to successful R&D operations, supporting accuracy, compliance, and innovation. But as the number of compounds being handled in a lab grows, managing samples can become more challenging. In this new era, R&D is driven by increasingly complex experiments, calling for sample management practices that are built for such intricacy. As the number of variables and samples involved in experiments rises, so does the volume of data. In our 2024 State of Tech in Biotech report , 87% of biotech leaders surveyed expected at least a 2x growth in R&D data within their teams alone this year. And because these teams are embracing new approaches to discover and develop drugs, not only are they generating exponentially more scientific data, but that data is increasingly fragmented as well. Managing samples effectively allows for better organization and integration of such, helping researchers make sense of large datasets and derive meaningful insights. The new era of science calls for more: more people, more data, and more technology. In our report, 53% of large-company respondents said they collaborate and share data with over 20 colleagues, so integrating data and teams becomes essential. Following the principles for effective sample management can help ensure that data is accurate, well-organized, and accessible, making it easier to correlate, share, and analyze results across experiments and studies. Principles for effective sample management It’s no question that managing samples effectively is critical for accurate, reliable experimental results. By sticking to the following principles, teams can ensure that their sample management practices support the integrity of their R&D activities — and avoid a dreaded experimental redo from a bad or lost sample. Accurate labels: Ensuring consistent, clear labels for all samples eliminates potential errors, while aiding in tracking and retrieval downstream. Best practice for identifying information includes criteria such as sample ID, date, time and any other relevant descriptors. Standard operating procedures (SOPs) : Establishing and adhering to standardized processes for each phase of sample management helps to further avoid inaccuracies. Inventory and data management : Integrating sample data with other data sources allows for more robust analysis. And by using inventory management systems to keep track of sample quantities, locations, and usage, the chances of sample loss or redundancy is greatly reduced. Collaboration and communication : Building the avenues for effective communication and collaboration across and within teams strengthens coordination for improved innovation. Continuous improvement : In order to scale your sample management practices, continuous review must occur. By auditing existing practices, opportunities arise to incorporate new technologies, address issues, and improve efficiency. Listening to your team, and seeking feedback from regular users, will contribute to the overall management process. To put this all into action, you need more than a crumpled printout taped to a fridge or an Excel sheet that rarely gets opened, let alone updated. You need a solution that serves as a digital window into your physical lab. In other words, a LIMS platform. From the bench to your inbox Our monthly newsletter features science insights, industry best practices, and stories from teams pushing biotech forward. LIMS for sample management A modern LIMS serves as a central productivity hub to manage lab data, workflows and teams, and increase lab operational efficiency, productivity and effectiveness in delivering results. A LIMS is a prime solution for sample management due to its ability to streamline and enhance many elements of laboratory operations. Serving as a centralized platform for data management, it allows teams to access and manage sample-related data in a single place. By streamlining these processes, a LIMS can enhance productivity, saving valuable time for high-value work. Here are a few specific ways that a LIMS can move the needle for managing samples: Efficient sample tracking: LIMS provides real-time tracking of samples, providing insight into status, location, and handling history. Customizable workflows: The flexibility LIMS affords ensures that workflows can fit the specific criteria of analyses and sample handling. Data security: Compliant with industry security standards, LIMS offers robust security features that keep sensitive data protected. Data integration: LIMS has interoperability with other laboratory systems, ensuring seamless data transfer and reducing the need for time-consuming manual data entry. Why companies love Benchling for sample management While there are many software applications that serve as point solutions, Benchling’s sample management solution gives you lab inventory management that’s intelligently connected with your entire R&D data– meaning you can see the entire historical context of a sample with a few clicks. With Benchling, R&D teams can optimize space usage, connect physical samples to their experimental context, and automate location tracking to ensure data integrity Benchling offers custom inventory management, chemical inventory, barcode integration, permissions and location tracking, so you don’t have to spend time hunting for reagents or samples. By interconnecting your samples, experimental results, and metadata, workflows become streamlined, allowing scientists to submit assay requests directly from input samples. title: Colaboração com fornecedores: como estabelecer e mensurar?
summary: Entenda o conceito de colaboração com fornecedores, os benefícios e 7 boas práticas para formar parcerias estratégicas com essas empresas!
body_text: A colaboração com fornecedores se refere à prática de trabalhar em estreita e contínua parceria com as empresas que compõem a rede de abastecimento de um negócio. Para tal, cria-se uma relação comercial que vai além de apenas comprar um produto ou contratar um serviço e pagar pelo recebimento. Inclusive, a cooperação na cadeia de suprimentos é uma forma de os envolvidos crescerem de maneira sustentável e com alto potencial lucrativo. Segundo a McKinsey & Company , organizações que colaboram regularmente com seus fornecedores têm crescimento e rentabilidade maiores e custos operacionais reduzidos. Além disso, formar uma parceria estratégica com fornecedores ajuda a mitigar risco e a fortalecer a cadeia de suprimentos, pois constrói relações mais sólidas e confiáveis. Achou interessante e quer resultados como esses na sua empresa? Então, siga a leitura para entender tudo sobre a estratégia. O que contempla a colaboração com fornecedores? A colaboração com fornecedores é um conceito que leva o relacionamento comercial a outro patamar. O motivo é que promove a construção de um vínculo profundo de contribuição mútua e alinhamento de objetivos e estratégias com foco em crescimento de longo prazo para os envolvidos. Porém, para chegar a esse nível, é preciso basear a gestão colaborativa de fornecedores em pilares como: comprometimento : tanto quem contrata quanto quem fornece precisa dedicar tempo e atenção iguais ao relacionamento comercial. Essa dedicação pode incluir sugestões de novas tecnologias e adequações aos processos, por exemplo; comunicação : por meio de diálogos sinceros, transparentes, respeitosos e próximos, mas sem perder o profissionalismo. É essencial evitar ruídos e falas que gerem desentendimentos; compartilhamento de metas : ajuda a alinhar expectativas, o entendimento dos planos e objetivos do parceiro comercial e a garantir o mesmo foco; melhoria contínua : a qual se pode obter com, por exemplo, sugestões de ajustes em etapas ineficientes e revisões periódicas na forma de aquisição e entrega; flexibilidade : essencial para facilitar ajustes decorrentes das novas necessidades do mercado, mudanças de comportamento dos consumidores, ou ritmo de crescimento das empresas envolvidas; resolução de problemas : de modo que ambas as partes se beneficiem das soluções e se protejam, sem gerar delegação negativa de responsabilidade ou culpa. Dica! Aproveite e leia também: “ Como e por que criar relacionamentos duradouros com fornecedores? ” Quais são os benefícios da colaboração com fornecedores? Estes são os principais benefícios da colaboração com fornecedores: promoção de inovação conjunta; redução de custos operacionais; diminuição de erros; ganho de eficiência e agilidade nos processos e fluxos; aumento da qualidade do fornecimento e, por consequência, dos produtos/serviços entregues aos clientes finais; elevação do poder competitivo por conta da vantagem anterior; mitigação de riscos , como os de desabastecimento, jurídico e financeiro. Esses são benefícios possíveis de alcançar com a construção de uma parceria estratégica com fornecedores devido aos pilares que citamos. Afinal, a junção de uma boa comunicação, alinhamento de expectativas e colaboração mútua é o segredo para formar um relacionamento comercial no qual as partes envolvidas realmente ganham. Sugestão de leitura: “ Benefícios da gestão de fornecedores: 7 que mais se destacam! ” 7 boas práticas para uma parceria estratégica com fornecedores Se você pretende firmar uma parceria estratégica com os fornecedores que atendem à sua empresa, nossa dica é aplicar estas boas práticas: garanta o entendimento do valor da parceria; adote a cultura do feedback; defina SLAs; estabeleça um fluxo de compartilhamento de informações; tenha planos de contingência; promova treinamentos e capacitações; use ferramentas de gestão. Vamos aos detalhes? 1. Garanta o entendimento do valor da parceria O valor em uma colaboração com fornecedores não se refere a preços e custos, mas, sim, ao reconhecimento do quanto cada um pode ganhar além de questões relacionadas ao dinheiro . Como exemplos, benefícios como descoberta de novas tecnologias, aprimoramento de conhecimento técnico, chance de aumentar a qualidade e de melhorar a eficiência operacional. Inclusive, esses pontos refletem positivamente na formação de outras parcerias comerciais. 2. Adote a cultura do feedback A cultura do feedback consiste em criar um fluxo de comunicação fluido e contínuo para fazer apontamentos positivos e solicitar melhorias, mas também recebê-los . Essa prática reforça a cooperação na cadeia de suprimentos porque abre espaço para diálogos sinceros, que ajudam tanto a empresa fornecedora quanto a contratante a aprimorar suas atuações e crescerem. Este artigo também ajudará você: “ O que é desenvolvimento de fornecedores? Como fazer com eficiência? ” 3. Defina SLAs SLA é a sigla de Service Level Agreement, que, em português, quer dizer Acordo de Nível de Serviço. Trata-se de um contrato que estabelece responsabilidades e parâmetros de atendimento em uma parceria comercial. No SLA, estão diretrizes, normas, metas e critérios que ambas as partes devem obrigatoriamente seguir. No caso de uma gestão colaborativa de fornecedores, pode-se incluir instruções como prazo de entrega das mercadorias e de resposta a e-mails e mensagens de pós-venda. 4. Estabeleça um fluxo de compartilhamento de informações Defina quem são os responsáveis por atender cada fornecedor e o canal oficial para envio de pedidos de compras e documentos, por exemplo. Para troca de informações diárias, é possível usar ferramentas corporativas como o Slack e o WhatsApp Business, desde que haja um fluxo estabelecido de respostas e um SLA para esses meios de comunicação. 5. Tenha planos de contingência Por mais que a parceria estratégica com fornecedores seja confiável, ambos os lados estão passíveis a enfrentar situações inesperadas. A fim de não comprometer esse relacionamento, construído pouco a pouco diariamente, defina planos de contingência para variados cenários — por exemplo, determine o que seu time de compras deve fazer quando o fornecedor avisar que não consegue atender à nova demanda por problemas pontuais com um maquinário. Ter uma “rota de fuga” previamente estabelecida evita complicações, interrupção no seu fluxo operacional e, principalmente, desentendimento com o fornecedor estratégico. 6. Promova treinamentos e capacitações Os treinamentos para a equipe de compras são importantes para manter os funcionários atualizados sobre a chegada de novas tecnologias, mudanças no segmento, leis, normas e novas estratégias de compras. Ao promover a capacitação dos fornecedores, você os ajuda a entender como sua empresa funciona e, dessa forma, compreender melhor quais são as necessidades de abastecimento do seu negócio. 7. Use ferramentas de gestão Ferramentas de gestão de fornecedores, como um SRM (Supplier Relationship Management) , ajudam a alcançar a cooperação na cadeia de suprimentos por facilitarem a comunicação, gerar dados para monitoramento de desempenho e automatizar diversos processos. Com o SRM da Linkana , por exemplo, você envia ao fornecedor um convite para acessar o nosso portal para responder questionários e enviar documentos privados. Dica! Assista ao vídeo abaixo e veja como esse fluxo funciona, na prática! Como mensurar a colaboração e o relacionamento com fornecedores? Para confirmar se o relacionamento com os fornecedores gerou a colaboração esperada, você deve mensurar alguns aspectos. Para essa atividade, use indicadores-chave como: conformidade com prazos de entrega; taxa de resolução de problemas; nível de serviço ao cliente (SLAs cumpridos) tempo médio de resposta às solicitações eficiência logística (Lead Time de entrega) nível de transparência e compartilhamento de informações. A escolha dos indicadores depende do que você quer mensurar e acompanhar. Gostou de saber como promover a colaboração com fornecedores? E por que não estabelecer uma cooperação mútua logo no início da parceria? A melhor forma é identificar as empresas fornecedoras certas nas primeiras etapas . body_text:
InterDigital 2024 Year-End Newsletter December 2024 InterDigital Comms

As we close out 2024, we reflect on a year of exceptional milestones, underpinned by our innovative spirit, strategic partnerships, industry leadership, and continued research in wireless, video, and AI. This newsletter spotlights InterDigital’s achievements of the past year.

2024 Spotlight on InterDigital

InterDigital delivered strong financial results throughout 2024, driven by high-value licensing agreements and a robust patent portfolio shaped by our foundational research and innovation. In addition to exceeding revenue expectations in Q3, and announcing a 2030 revenue target of $1B annually, InterDigital hosted its first Investor Day under current management, featuring presentations by President and CEO Liren Chen and members of the executive team outlining InterDigital’s mission and vision.

The year was also punctuated by strategic licensing successes, including new patent license agreements with Samsung, Google, Lenovo, and TPV. InterDigital also renewed and signed new license agreements with Panasonic, covering our 4G, 5G, cellular, HEVC video, and Wi-Fi patents. In 2024, we signed a landmark license agreement with OPPO Group, which includes OPPO, realme, and OnePlus, marking a trend that reinforces the foundational nature of our research and innovation to the mobile ecosystem.

In 2024, we expanded our reach in different ways, hiring Ken Kaskoun as InterDigital’s Chief Growth Officer, leveraging his experience at Qualcomm and SomaLogic and background as an engineer, lawyer, and experienced inventor to drive InterDigital’s growth and technological prowess in wireless, video, and AI. InterDigital also opened a new office location in Melville, Long Island in addition to celebrating more than ten years of research and innovation in our London office. InterDigital also announced several academic partnerships to amplify our research, including joining Princeton University’s Next G Initiative and collaborating with Concordia University’s Intelligent Next Generation Networking and Multimedia (IN2GM) Lab on AI-enabled immersive media delivery.

A full scope of our research ingenuity, social impact, and environmental “handprint” was outlined in our 2024 Corporate Sustainability report, including an update on our commitment to DEI. Among the events hosted throughout the year, InterDigital’s inaugural Women’s Network hosted a Fireside Chat with Board members Jean Rankin, Joan Gillman, and our Chief Licensing Officer Eeva Hakoranta to discuss inclusive ways of working and advocacy for women in technology.

InterDigital's Leadership and Awards

Our impact is bolstered by the ability of our research to advance wireless and video capabilities, and by the expertise and leadership of the outstanding engineers and experts who drive our innovation.

  • This year, InterDigital named Michael Starsinic and Fabrice Le Léannec as Inventors of the Year. The outstanding engineers were recognized for their expertise and research contributions to wireless and video standards that make seamless communication of data and content across a variety of devices, services, and network capabilities possible.
  • InterDigital CEO Liren Chen was also appointed to the USPTO’s Council for Inclusive Innovation to help drive greater participation in America’s innovation economy, and Chief Licensing Officer Eeva Hakoranta has been named among the 50 most influential people in IP by Managing IP.
  • At IEEE, Dong Tian was elevated to IEEE Fellow and Xiaofei Wang was appointed Chair of the 802.11 Standing Committee on Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning. Yifan Li was also selected as the Philadelphia Section Delaware Valley Young Electrical Engineer of the Year.
  • In 3GPP, Atle Monrad was elected to Chair of SA6 - Service and Systems Aspects Working Group and at the ITU, Gaelle Martin-Cocher was re-elected to Vice Chair the Telecommunication Standardization Advisory Group (TSAG).
  • In the U.S., Doug Castor was elected to Co-Chair the ATIS Next G Alliance Steering Group, and Bob Gazda was invited to participate in the FCC Communications Security, Reliability, and Interoperability Council (CSRIC IX).

In addition to earned leadership roles, InterDigital also received several awards recognizing our outstanding research and innovation.

  • According to Lexis Nexis, InterDigital has been listed for three consecutive years on the Innovation Momentum: Global Top 100 report and was ranked among the top five patent owners in HEVC/VVC and Wi-Fi 6 when combining both quality and quantity.
  • In 2024, InterDigital was awarded two CSI Awards for Best Immersive Video and Video Processing Technology, and shortlisted for an award for best sustainability project.
  • InterDigital engineers were also awarded the SMPTE 2024 Journal Certificate of Merit for outstanding research on Pixel Value Reduction technologies.
  • In wireless, InterDigital was shortlisted for three FierceNetwork Innovation awards for outstanding innovation in AI, wireless evolution, and sustainability.

InterDigital's Industry Engagement and Demonstrations

Throughout the year, InterDigital demonstrated technology, presented expertise, and showcased research collaborations at conferences and industry events around the world.

Mobile World Congress

At MWC:

  • InterDigital demonstrated a snapshot of our innovation impact, spotlighting a suite of 6G sensing and energy-aware HDR solutions, and haptics codecs that empower connected experiences at work, at rest, and at play.
  • InterDigital showcased alongside industry partners to amplify our research, including hosting a joint demo with Razer to enable a live, haptic-enhanced racing game experience. InterDigital also collaborated with Broadpeak to display MPEG V3C immersive content distribution over a content delivery network and partnered with Keysight to show how AI channel estimators can be trained, added to a 6G physical layer, and validated with over-the-air hardware.
  • In addition to demos, Valérie Allié delivered a stage presentation on innovations enabling immersive streaming experiences, explaining the potential and pathway towards delivering immersive video experiences enhanced by haptics at scale.
  • Later in the year, Bill Redmann spoke on a panel exploring technologies and solutions to support more immersive sports and fan experiences at MWC Las Vegas.

Video Conferences

Our video engineers also promoted our video innovation and impacts at a variety of tradeshows, including AWE, NAB, and IBC.

  • At AWE, InterDigital and Philips demonstrated volumetric streaming technologies empowering immersive sports experiences, specifically implementations of the MPEG Visual Volumetric Video-based Coding (V3C) standard.
  • At NAB, InterDigital showcased innovations in high definition and sustainable video streaming alongside partners from ATSC, Advanced HDR by Technicolor, and the Ultra HD Forum. InterDigital specifically displayed contributions to Advanced HDR streaming solutions and energy-aware media solutions like Pixel Value Reduction.
  • At IBC, InterDigital displayed our innovative research in broadcast and immersive video solutions alongside industry partners at the Ultra HD Forum and International Association of Broadcasting Manufacturers (IAMB) booths, and promoted our contributions to the MPEG Visual Volumetric Video-based Coding (V3C) Immersive Platform at the 5G-MAG Insights conference.

Wireless Conferences

In wireless, our engineers amplified their expertise through different industry trade shows and conferences, like the 6GSymposium and the Brooklyn 6G Summit.

  • InterDigital returned as a partner to the 6GSymposium Fall, which featured panel presentations and discussions with InterDigital’s CTO Rajesh Pankaj, VP and Head of Wireless Labs Milind Kulkarni, and Head of Wireless Research Doug Castor exploring the crucial conversations and most compelling use cases for the ‘next G’ and the global standards ushering in new wireless capabilities and services.
  • At the Brooklyn 6G Summit, InterDigital and The University of Texas at Austin demonstrated their collaboration to validate AI solutions for wireless networks and shape AI for 6G.

InterDigital's Expertise

Throughout the year, InterDigital publishes reports, eBooks, blogs, and other content outlining our research priorities while our experts contribute their expertise to the understanding of advancements and innovation in wireless, video, and AI.

Wireless

Building upon our heritage of wireless research, innovation, and standards contributions, we explored the current state of wireless evolution and introduced the critical technologies and trends shaping 5G Advanced and the road to 6G.

  • InterDigital’s white paper with ABI Research on Driving 5G-Advanced to 6G explores how 5G-Advanced is revealing new enterprise capabilities and paving the way for 6G. Experts shared their expertise in a webinar that discussed the benefits and impact of 6G-enabling technology ISAC for new services, verticals, and enterprises.
  • In addition to our report and webinar, InterDigital’s expertise was quoted in CNBC discussing network slicing as a crucial step in the technological upgrades leading to 5G-Advanced, and in a Telecoms.com article about the telecoms operators efforts to recoup investments in 5G infrastructure. InterDigital shared some insights with IBC on the mobile industry’s search for breakthrough applications and enterprise use cases for 5G, and was interviewed in Light Reading for our expertise on reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RIS) and higher frequency bands as potential breakthroughs for 6G.
  • To foster a deeper understanding of ISAC, an important 6G enabling technology where InterDigital leads innovation, we published an eBook explaining the convergence of telecom and sensing data through ISAC and the emerging use cases for network operators and users alike. Our engineers further detailed the benefits and challenges of ISAC, and were positioned as leaders advancing 6G sensing capabilities in Fierce Network.
  • InterDigital was recognized in 6GWorld for our role in 6G innovation and fostering ISAC’s potential to supplement fixed broadband, and Alain Mourad was featured in The Fast Mode explaining how ISAC paves the way for smart factory implementation.
  • Throughout the year, Doug Castor contributed to a deeper understanding of the 6G roadmap and the technology trends, limitations, and milestones that will define 6G, including in this 6GWorld webinar. Milind Kulkarni elaborated upon the roadmap and outlined the direction 6G standardization is taking and goals for 6G research with 6GWorld.

Video

InterDigital also drives research and innovation in video as our engineers develop codecs and associated media solutions targeting 2D and immersive video. Our research continues to enhance how the world communicates by enabling video experiences to be crisper, more immersive, and more realistic.

  • InterDigital’s white paper with Futuresource Consulting on Haptics: The Next Modality in Immersive Entertainment detailed the standards, device enhancements, and innovation in content capture and creation that are opening new opportunities for immersive entertainment, and specifically the efforts to integrate haptics, or the sense of touch, within immersive communications. Our expert webinar discussed the state of the haptic market, standards ecosystem, and use cases that leverage haptic-enhanced communications and experiences.
  • In addition to Philippe Guillotel’s feature in Forbes on the ways haptics may augment our lives in the future, InterDigital’s Immersive Video team posted informative articles to introduce the innovative devices and standards efforts to bring interoperable haptic-enhanced immersive experiences to a wider audience and to outline the immersive video codecs that are encouraging new depths of immersion in our connected experiences.
  • 2024 was also deemed the “summer of sports” with the Paris Olympics and Euro Games attracting huge global audiences streaming the sporting events to their phones, telephones, and other devices. Exploring the ways InterDigital’s research and innovation might impact sports and Olympic viewing experiences in the future, InterDigital’s video experts were featured in articles in CSI Magazine, TVBEurope, Advanced Television, FEED Magazine, and more to offer expert guidance on the myriad ways advancements in video, XR, and 6G might immerse them deeper within the action.

AI

Alongside innovations in wireless and video, InterDigital showcased our research expertise in AI, including its practical applications for both video and wireless.

  • When exploring the practical applications of AI, Fabien Racapé and Hyomin Choi penned a blog introducing the topic of video compression for machines and the new standards and delivery mechanisms to process video content intended for machine and algorithm consumption.
  • Fabien Racapé also discussed with Streaming Media InterDigital’s CompressAI platform for integrating AI with video codec development and its role in accelerating AI-based codec design.
  • In addition to the AI channel estimator demo InterDigital hosted with Keysight, Ulises Olvera-Hernandez was also quoted in a Capacity article exploring AI’s transformative impact on communication networks, highlighting AI’s role in creating dynamic networks, reducing energy consumption, enhancing user experiences, and fortifying security protocols.

Sustainability and More

We also strongly consider the ways our research, innovation, and standards contributions impact and empower society.

  • On Earth Day, InterDigital shared the way our research and innovation encourage greater energy awareness, and Stéphane Tronchon discussed how standards will help us achieve a more sustainable future.
  • Elsewhere, Valérie Allié’s feature in FEED Magazine introduces solutions to make Ultra HD content more sustainable, and her interview with TVBEurope outlined how Advanced HDR solutions can reduce energy consumption.
  • In addition to being interviewed by the Schwab Network, and profiled in Forbes for leading one of the world’s largest pure research companies, managing innovative teams and high-powered partnerships, InterDigital CEO Liren Chen reiterated the importance of open, global standards in helping new entrants in a market and open new opportunities for incumbents.

As we reflect on a robust year of milestones and achievement, we take great pride in our accomplishments and will continue our important and impactful work as we enter 2025. From InterDigital, we wish you a happy and healthy new year.

title: What Is an SMS Gateway and How Does It Work?
summary: In this guide, explore what an SMS gateway is, how it works, and why businesses rely on it for bulk messaging, marketing, and customer engagement.
body_text: Text messaging is a highly effective tool for businesses, with SMS boasting a 98% global delivery rate. This reliability makes it ideal for reaching customers quickly and consistently. However, managing high volumes of customer communications manually can be challenging for businesses. An SMS gateway makes it possible for a broader range of devices and applications to communicate with each other. Whether you want to launch a marketing campaign, send automated alerts, or engage in two-way conversations with customers, an SMS gateway simplifies the process. Using SMS gateway services, you can send a message from your computer to a phone (or vice versa). In this guide, we’ll dive into how SMS gateway providers work, the different applications of SMS gateway services, and how you can choose the right provider for your business’ needs. So, let’s begin! What is an SMS gateway? An SMS gateway is a technology that allows software applications or computers to send text messages to mobile phones. Often, messages sent from a computer are not in a format that’s compatible with SMS. In such cases, SMS gateways serve as translators, converting the message into a format that mobile devices can understand. The main job of an SMS gateway is to ensure the message is compatible with mobile networks. Businesses use SMS gateways to send bulk text messages to customers directly from a computer or software platform. Interestingly, SMS gateway services can also work in reverse, allowing mobile users to send messages back to computers. While previously SMS gateways were offered as physical hardware with SIM cards and embedded radios, businesses and consumers no longer need hardware-based solutions today. Instead, they use cloud-based systems that seamlessly translate and transmit messages. These advancements are powered by SMS APIs , which allow messages to be delivered to specific devices at the right time, without the need for physical hardware. How does SMS gateway technology work? Here’s a simple step-by-step breakdown of how modern SMS gateway services operate: Create the message : Compose your text message within your business application. Send via API : The message is sent to the SMS gateway through an SMS API . Convert the message : The gateway uses protocols like HTTP or SMPP (Short Message Peer-to-Peer) to format the message for mobile networks. Protocols like SMPP play a key role in the smooth operation of SMS gateways. They enable fast and reliable communication between the gateway and mobile carriers, ensuring your messages reach their destination promptly — even during high-volume campaigns. Route the message : The gateway forwards the message to the appropriate telecom carrier. Deliver the message : The telecom carrier ensures the text reaches the recipient’s phone. Confirm delivery : The SMS gateway receives a delivery report from the carrier and relays it back to your application, confirming the message was received. Imagine you’re running SMS marketing campaigns and want to send a promotional text to all your customers. Your audience is spread across the U.S., using different carriers like AT&T, Verizon, or T-Mobile. Instead of dealing with each network separately, an SMS gateway simplifies the process. You connect once, and the gateway handles the rest — distributing your message to everyone at the same time, no matter which network they’re on. Types of SMS gateways When it comes to SMS marketing campaigns, two types of SMS gateways are most commonly used: Email to SMSThis type of gateway converts email messages into SMS format , ensuring they meet the technical requirements for mobile delivery. It’s a two-way system, allowing businesses to send text messages to email inboxes and receive replies in return. Web to SMSFrequently used by application-to-person SMS platforms, this gateway connects mobile phones with web applications. It enables businesses to send both SMS and MMS messages directly from a web application to recipients’ mobile devices. Web to SMS gateways are more feature-rich than other options, offering enhanced flexibility and functionality. Applications of SMS gateways SMS gateways have a wide range of applications for businesses and organizations, enabling them to communicate quickly and effectively with their customers. Here are some use cases: Marketing campaigns SMS marketing is a powerful tool for businesses to connect directly with their customers. It allows you to send promotional messages, special offers, and important updates right to your customers' mobile phones. According to the 2023 Mobile Consumer Trends Report , SMS is a preferred communication channel for 52% of customers , making SMS an essential part of any marketing strategy. A great example of effective SMS marketing is GoCheckin, an app developed by Fastboy Marketing. GoCheckin helps beauty salons send appointment reminders and promotional messages to their clients. Fastboy uses Plivo as their communication platform and SMS gateway provider to efficiently handle high SMS volumes, ensuring seamless message delivery. This switch made it easier for Fastboy to send texts without requiring customers to download an app. Customer engagement Text message gateways boost customer engagement by enabling businesses to send timely and personalized alerts and notifications. Common use cases: Appointment reminders Appointment reminders are a highly effective way to engage customers and reduce no-shows. Once you integrate an SMS API into your existing systems, when a trigger event occurs, for example, an appointment reminder, the system will communicate with the SMS gateway. The gateway then processes and sends the message to the customer's mobile network within seconds. For example, a dental clinic could automatically send reminders to patients a day before their appointments, increasing the likelihood of attendance. Customer feedback requests SMS gateways make it easy for businesses to request feedback after a purchase or service interaction. For instance, a restaurant might send a text asking customers to rate their dining experience. This provides valuable insights to help businesses improve. Notifications and alerts Automated notifications and account alerts keep customers informed and build trust. SMS is particularly effective for delivering quick and reliable updates about orders, security alerts, or account changes. Businesses like ecommerce platforms use SMS to keep customers updated at every stage of their order process. For instance, Luxer One , a California-based company that provides secure package lockers for residential properties, uses SMS to send package delivery notifications. Previously relying on email, they found many residents overlooked or missed their emails, leading to uncollected packages and dissatisfaction. By switching to SMS, Luxer One achieved over 99% consistent delivery, improving customer satisfaction and the package pickup experience. Similarly, Deckers , a footwear giant, uses SMS to keep customers informed about their order and delivery statuses. After placing an order, customers receive real-time shipment updates via text until the package arrives. This transparency reduced track-package inquiries by 15–20% annually, significantly enhancing the overall customer experience. Why should businesses use SMS gateways?
